title: How Do Shared Ownership Mortgage Brokers Work?
h1: Not revealed by search results. Title tag confirmed identically in [a] and [b] as 'How Do Shared Ownership Mortgage Brokers Work?'; the H1 is presumably the same but was not shown.
summary: Page type: blog article (not a case study). Thesis as revealed by snippets: shared ownership lets a home-buyer purchase a share in a property while paying rent on the remaining unowned share (the search tool's summary [a] attributes a 'usually 25% to 75%' share range to the page); because shared ownership mortgages 'differ from traditional mortgages in a number of ways' and not all lenders offer them, borrowers should understand the product first and an independent mortgage broker is useful. Concrete guidance revealed, i.e. what the broker does: (1) checks whether the buyer meets the criteria set by housing associations and lenders; (2) finds lenders that actually offer shared ownership products, since 'not all mortgage lenders offer shared ownership products, but a broker has access to a broad range of options'; (3) ensures all financial documentation is prepared correctly to improve approval chances; (4) explains how to increase ownership later (staircasing). NOT revealed: fees, rates, deposit figures, named lenders or housing associations, eligibility thresholds, FAQ, author, publication date, calls to action, meta description.
